adya-00: Om — salutations to Adya, the Primordial.
adya-01: Listen, child — I speak the Adya Stotram of great fruit. Whoever recites it always with devotion becomes dear to Vishnu.
adya-02: In Kali yuga that person has not the least fear of death or disease. A childless woman, listening for three fortnights, obtains a child.
adya-03: Heard from a brahmana's mouth for two months — release from bondage. A woman whose children die, listening six months, bears living children.
adya-04: Recited on a boat, in distress, or in battle — one attains victory. Written and kept in the house — no fear of fire or thieves.
adya-05: Ever victorious before kings; all gods are pleased. Om Hrīm — She is Brahmani in Brahmaloka, Sarvamangala in Vaikuntha.
adya-06: Indrani in Amaravati, Ambika in Varuna's house, Kalarupa in Yama's world, Shubha in Kubera's dwelling.
adya-07: Mahananda in the fire-quarter, Mrigavahini in the wind-quarter, Raktadanta in the southwest, Shuladharini in the northeast.
adya-08: Vaishnavi in the netherworld, Devamohini in Lanka-isle (Simhala), Surasa in Manidvipa, Bhadrakalika in Lanka.
adya-09: Rameshvari at Setubandha, Vimala at Purushottama (Puri), Viraja in Odra, Kamakshi on the blue mountain.
adya-10: Kalika in Bengal, Maheshvari in Ayodhya, Annapurna in Varanasi, Gayeshvari in Gaya.
adya-11: Bhadrakali in Kurukshetra, Katyayani in Vraja, Mahamaya in Dvaraka, Maheshvari in Mathura.
adya-12: You are the hunger of all beings and the tide of the ocean; You are shukla navami and the supreme krishna ekadashi.
adya-13: Daughter of Daksha, destroyer of Daksha's sacrifice; You are Rama's Janaki, who caused Ravana's fall.
adya-14: Slayer of Chanda and Munda, destroyer of Raktabija, crusher of Nishumbha and Shumbha, killer of Madhu and Kaitabha.
adya-15: Durga who grants devotion to Vishnu, always giver of joy and liberation. Whoever constantly recites this sacred hymn to Adya —
adya-16: No fear of any fever; all disease is destroyed; the fruit of a crore of tirthas is obtained — of this there is no doubt.
adya-17: May Jaya guard me in front, Vijaya behind; Narayani at the head, Simhavahini over every limb.
adya-18: On every limb Shivaduti, Ugrachanda, Parameshvari; Vishalakshi, Mahamaya, Kaumari, Shankhini, Shiva.
adya-19: Chakrini, Jayadhatri, battle-intoxicated, lover of war, Durga, Jayanti, Kali, Bhadrakali, Mahodari.
adya-20: Narasimhi, Varahi, giver of siddhi and joy, terrifying, greatly fierce, destroyer of great fear.
adya-21: Om, salutations to Adya, thrice. Thus ends the Adya Stotram in the Brahma Yamala, dialogue of Brahma and Narada.
